text: Plumb must keep three artifacts in sync: the spec (markdown files), tests (pytest suite), and code (implementation).
Plumb must be installable via both pip and uv with package name 'plumb-dev' and CLI command 'plumb'.
The plumb init command must check that the current directory is a git repository and exit with error if not.
The plumb init command must create the .plumb/ directory if it does not exist.
The plumb init command must prompt the user to provide a path to spec file(s) and validate that the path exists and contains .md files.
The plumb init command must prompt the user to provide a path to test file(s) and validate that the path exists.
The plumb init command must run pytest --collect-only to verify tests can be collected and fail fast with SystemExit(1) on collection failure.
The plumb init command must write .plumb/config.json with spec_paths, test_paths, claude_log_path, initialized_at, last_commit, and last_commit_branch fields.
The plumb init command must create a .plumbignore file in the project root if it does not exist.
The plumb init command must install the git pre-commit hook by writing a script to .git/hooks/pre-commit and setting it as executable.
The plumb init command must install the Claude Code skill locally by copying plumb/skill/SKILL.md to .claude/skills/plumb/SKILL.md in the project root.
The plumb init command must append a Plumb status block to CLAUDE.md at the project root, creating it if it does not exist.
The plumb init command must run plumb parse-spec to do an initial parse of the spec into requirements.
The plumb init command must print a confirmation summary including confirmation that the skill was installed at .claude/skills/plumb/SKILL.md.
Tests must support comment-based markers using # plumb:req-XXXXXXXX format for linking to requirements.
Tests must support function name-based linking using test_req_XXXXXXXX_ format for linking to requirements.
The plumb hook command must read .plumb/config.json and exit 0 silently if not found.
The plumb hook command must get the current staged diff via git diff --cached.
The plumb hook command must get the current branch name.
The plumb hook command must detect amends by comparing HEAD commit's parent SHA to last_commit and delete decisions with matching commit_sha before re-running analysis.
The plumb hook command must detect broken references by checking all SHAs in decisions.jsonl against git history and flagging unreachable SHAs with ref_status: broken.
The plumb hook command must run the Diff Analysis DSPy program on the staged diff.
The plumb hook command must locate and read the Claude Code conversation log if available, reading turns since last_commit timestamp.
The plumb hook command must support reading Claude Code native session files from ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-uuid>.jsonl.
The plumb hook command must merge conversation turns from all relevant session files modified after last_commit and sort chronologically.
The plumb hook command must convert tool_use blocks to '[tool: Name] description' format in conversation turns.
The plumb hook command must filter out decisions marked as non-spec-relevant before creating Decision records.
The plumb hook command must merge and deduplicate decisions across chunks using DuckDB for cross-shard queries.
The plumb hook command must check deduplication against all existing decisions (both pending and resolved) instead of only resolved ones.
The plumb hook command must implement within-batch similarity deduplication to compare new decisions against each other using Jaccard similarity check.
The plumb hook command must run Question Synthesizer for each decision with no associated question.
The plumb hook command must write all new decisions with status: pending to decisions.jsonl using branch-specific decision log files.
The plumb hook command must run plumb parse-spec to update requirements cache for any modified spec files.
The plumb hook command must batch spec updates across all decisions instead of running spec update for each individual decision.
The plumb hook command must use search-and-replace pairs pattern for spec updates with {old_text, new_text} operations.
The plumb hook command must implement a two-tier approach for spec updates: Tier 1 for existing section updates and Tier 2 for structural changes.
The plumb hook command must use outline-first approach for structural changes where LLM returns updated header outline first, then fills in content for new sections.
The plumb hook command must check whether it is running in a TTY (interactive terminal) or as a subprocess.
The plumb hook command must print a human-readable summary of pending decisions in TTY mode with instructions to run plumb review.
The plumb hook command must print a machine-readable JSON object to stdout in non-TTY mode (subprocess) containing pending_decisions count and array of decision objects.
The plumb hook command must exit non-zero when pending decisions exist.
The plumb hook command must exit 0 when no pending decisions exist after updating last_commit and last_commit_branch in config.json.
The plumb hook command must never exit non-zero due to an internal Plumb error; failures must print a warning to stderr and exit 0.
The plumb hook command must validate API access before proceeding with analysis and exit non-zero to block the commit if authentication fails.
The plumb hook command must raise a custom PlumbAuthError exception that alerts the user and provides clear instructions to set API key via environment variable or .env file.
The plumb hook --dry-run option must run full hook analysis on staged changes without writing to decisions.jsonl and always exit 0.
The plumb diff command must read staged changes via git diff --cached.
The plumb diff command must run Diff Analysis on the staged diff.
The plumb diff command must read and chunk the conversation log (turns since last_commit) if available.
The plumb diff command must run Decision Extraction per chunk.
The plumb diff command must print a preview to the terminal with summary of staged code changes, estimated number of decisions, and brief description of each estimated decision.
The plumb diff command must make no writes to .plumb/.
The plumb review command must read .plumb/decisions.jsonl and filter for status == pending.
The plumb review command must accept an optional --branch <name> flag to filter by branch.
The plumb review command must print 'No pending decisions.' and exit 0 if no pending decisions exist.
The plumb review command must display for each pending decision: framing question, decision made, branch, file and line references, ref_status, and most related spec text.
The plumb review command must prompt the user with [a]pprove, [r]eject, [e]dit, or [s]kip options.
The plumb review command must run plumb sync after all decisions are resolved.
The plumb review command must default spec_relevant field to True to ensure decisions pass through for user review when LLM classification is uncertain.
The plumb approve <id> command must update decision status to approved in decisions.jsonl.
The plumb approve <id> command must run plumb sync for that decision only.
The plumb approve command must support --all flag to approve multiple pending decisions efficiently.
The plumb approve command must display status with visual bar chart representation for coverage statistics using Rich.
The plumb approve command must use Rich's Status spinner that updates in-place for progress indication.
The plumb reject <id> --reason <text> command must update decision status to rejected and record the reason.
The plumb reject <id> --reason <text> command must not modify code or spec.
The plumb edit <id> <new decision text> command must replace the decision text with user-provided text.
The plumb edit <id> <new decision text> command must update status to edited.
The plumb edit <id> <new decision text> command must run plumb sync for that decision only.
The plumb modify <id> command must verify that status == rejected.
The plumb modify <id> command must read the staged diff and the decision object.
The plumb modify <id> command must call the Claude API with staged diff, decision, rejection reason, current spec, and instruction to modify code.
The plumb modify <id> command must apply proposed modification to staged files.
The plumb modify <id> command must run pytest to verify tests still pass after modification.
The plumb modify <id> command must stage modified files and update decision status to rejected_modified if tests pass.
The plumb modify <id> command must not stage the modification and update decision status to rejected_manual if tests fail.
The plumb modify <id> command must return a machine-readable JSON result in non-TTY mode with id, result, tests_passed, and diff fields.
The plumb modify <id> command must never commit the modification; only stage it.
The plumb sync command must add early exit check to avoid expensive operations when no unsynced decisions exist.
The plumb sync command must read decisions from decisions.jsonl with status approved or edited that have not yet been synced.
The plumb sync command must run WholeFileSpecUpdater for each spec file processing all decisions affecting that file together.
The plumb sync command must run OutlineMerger when new_sections is non-empty to determine proper positioning of new sections.
The plumb sync command must write updated spec file to disk using temp file → rename pattern.
The plumb sync command must fix newline formatting by ensuring proper newlines between section headers and body content.
The plumb sync command must run Test Generator to generate organized tests for requirements not covered by existing tests.
The plumb sync command must organize tests by functionality with proper requirement links in format test_<req_id>_<description>.
The plumb sync command must read only source files referenced by file_refs on synced decisions for context.
The plumb sync command must write generated tests to test_generated.py using temp file → rename pattern.
The plumb sync command must run plumb parse-spec to re-cache requirements.
The plumb sync command must set synced_at timestamp on each processed decision.
The plumb sync command must print a summary of spec sections updated and test files created.
The plumb sync command must use .plumbignore file with default patterns for documentation, build files, and IDE configurations.
The plumb sync command must identify and use the correct decision branch when marking decisions as synced.
The plumb parse-spec command must read all markdown files in spec_paths from config.json.
The plumb parse-spec command must run Requirement Parser on each file or paragraph block.
The plumb parse-spec command must assign each requirement a stable ID based on a hash of its content.
The plumb parse-spec command must write results to .plumb/requirements.json.
The plumb parse-spec command must preserve existing metadata including created_at and last_seen_commit timestamps for requirements with matching hashes.
The plumb parse-spec command must use regex patterns PLUMB_MARKER_RE and FUNC_NAME_RE to extract requirement IDs from test files for coverage mapping.
The plumb parse-spec command must process all requirements and AST summaries through CodeCoverageMapper using chunked mapping approach to avoid context overflow.
The plumb parse-spec command must use fan-out chunking to group source files under token budget (default 60000 tokens) and broadcast requirements to each chunk.
The plumb parse-spec command must implement granular per-file hashing with structured v2 cache format tracking individual requirement results.
The plumb parse-spec command must preserve existing incremental caching logic by applying chunking inside the LLM call after dirty requirements are determined.
The plumb parse-spec command must extract source file paths from evidence strings using pattern matching to determine requirement-to-file mappings.
The plumb parse-spec command must use greedy packing to group source/test summaries into chunks and ThreadPoolExecutor for concurrent chunk processing.
The plumb parse-spec command must merge results from multiple chunks using custom logic that ORs implemented flags and concatenates evidence strings per requirement_id.
The plumb coverage command must run pytest --cov and parse output to report line coverage percentage.
The plumb coverage command must check for each requirement whether a test references or maps to it using string-matching for requirement IDs.
The plumb coverage command must scan for link markers in test files to determine coverage.
The plumb coverage command must report count and percentage of requirements covered.
The plumb coverage command must print a formatted table using rich.
The plumb coverage command must use LLM calls to refresh the requirements cache for accurate coverage analysis.
The plumb coverage command must measure and report coverage improvement achieved by marker injection.
The plumb coverage command must display progress using an in-place updating spinner, then print final results table.
The plumb status command must print tracked spec files and total requirements.
The plumb status command must print number of tests.
The plumb status command must print pending decisions with branch breakdown if spanning multiple branches.
The plumb status command must print decisions with broken git references.
The plumb status command must print last sync commit.
The plumb status command must print coverage summary for all three dimensions.
The plumb status command must operate in cache-only mode to avoid making LLM calls.
Plumb must support loading environment variables from .env files using python-dotenv dependency.
The plumb init command must support ANTHROPIC_API_KEY configuration through both environment variables and .env files.
Plumb must integrate with git hooks to automatically trigger workflows based on repository events.
The .plumb/ directory must contain config.json, decisions.jsonl, and requirements.json files that should be committed to version control.
The DiffAnalyzer program must output change summaries with files_changed, summary, and change_type (feature, bugfix, refactor, test, spec, config, or other).
The DiffAnalyzer program must group related changes into logical units without inventing meaning.
The DecisionExtractor program must accept chunk and diff_summary inputs.
The DecisionExtractor program must output decision objects with question, decision, made_by (user or agent), confidence, and spec_relevant fields.
The DecisionExtractor program must parse and preserve full tool call data from transcripts with category, tool_name, file_path, and input fields.
The DecisionExtractor program must use agentsview's 9-category tool taxonomy to structure tool information.
The DecisionExtractor program must maintain truncated results for Bash and Edit operations.
The DecisionExtractor program must not extract trivial decisions (variable naming, import ordering).
The QuestionSynthesizer program must accept a decision object with no associated question as input.
The QuestionSynthesizer program must output a plain-English question framing the decision for a developer.
The RequirementParser program must accept markdown string as input.
The RequirementParser program must output requirement objects with text and ambiguous fields.
The RequirementParser program must produce atomic statements in active voice with no duplicates.
The RequirementParser program must flag vague statements with ambiguous: true.
The SpecUpdater program must accept spec_section (markdown) and decision (approved decision object) as inputs.
The SpecUpdater program must output updated markdown for that section capturing result of decision as natural requirement.
The SpecUpdater program must not reference the decision itself in the output.
The SpecUpdater program must preserve existing formatting.
The TestGenerator program must accept requirements (uncovered), existing_tests (file contents), and code_context (relevant source) as inputs.
The TestGenerator program must output runnable pytest test code as a Python string.
The TestGenerator program must use one function per requirement with descriptive names (test_<req_id>_<description>).
The TestGenerator program must generate tests with real assertions against actual code under test.
The TestGenerator program must not generate pytest.skip() or # TODO: implement comments.
The TestGenerator program must not overwrite existing tests.
The TestGenerator program must generate complete and runnable tests rather than stub files.
The TestGenerator program must use increased context limits to accommodate complete test code.
The CodeModifier program must use the Anthropic Claude SDK with claude-haiku-4-5 model and max_tokens set to 16000.
The CodeModifier program must accept staged diff, rejected decision, rejection reason, and current spec as inputs.
The CodeModifier program must output modified file contents that satisfy the rejection while remaining consistent with the spec.
The CodeModifier program must handle multiple content block types in response parsing.
Conversation chunking must use primary unit of one user turn plus all following assistant turns up to but not including the next user message.
Conversation chunking must split chunks exceeding 6,000 tokens at tool call boundaries.
Conversation chunking must split at midpoint of largest assistant turn if no tool call boundary exists.
Conversation chunking must prepend final assistant turn of previous chunk as header to next chunk for overlap.
Conversation chunking must replace tool result turns longer than 500 tokens with raw file reads with [file read: <filename>] notation.
Conversation chunking must properly parse and reassemble assistant messages spanning multiple JSONL entries.
Conversation chunks must include metadata with chunk_index, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, truncated, and turns fields.
The conversation log parser must preserve full tool call information from Claude Code transcripts.
The conversation log parser must handle Claude Code's type/message schema format.
The conversation log parser must convert tool usage blocks to text format '[tool: Name] description' for consistency.
The conversation log parser must skip assistant entries that contain 'thinking' blocks, have 'isSidechain: true', or have 'isMeta: true'.
The conversation log parser must work seamlessly across different repositories without requiring additional user setup.
The decision log must be append-only where existing lines are never modified in place.
The decision log must use latest-line-wins logic for status updates where the latest line for a given id is canonical.

Decision log entries must include id, status, question, decision, made_by, commit_sha, branch, ref_status, conversation_available, file_refs, related_requirement_ids, confidence, chunk_index, conversation_truncated, rejection_reason, user_note, synced_at, reviewed_at, and created_at fields.
Decision log datetime fields (created_at, synced_at, reviewed_at) must be stored and round-tripped as ISO-8601 strings.
Decision status values must be: pending, approved, edited, rejected, rejected_modified, or rejected_manual.
Decision ref_status values must be: ok or broken.
Decision made_by values must be: user (human stated or confirmed) or agent.
Decision commit_sha must be null until the commit lands and must be populated by the hook on the second pass.
The system must filter for spec-relevant content during decision extraction in both conversation analysis and diff analysis methods.
The system must implement semantic similarity checking to handle duplicate or similar decisions effectively.
Classification tasks must not generate reasoning traces to maintain optimal performance.
LLM-based deduplication must utilize Claude Haiku 4.5 as the designated model.
The deduplicate_decisions() function must accept a use_llm parameter that defaults to False for backward compatibility.
The deduplication function must include fallback handling for truncated or failed LLM responses by returning all candidates when LLM returns None.
The system must implement intelligent deduplication by first running Jaccard similarity filtering, then applying LLM deduplication as second pass when 2 or more candidates remain.
The system must use DSPy's context manager with Haiku LM for deduplication while preserving Sonnet for other operations.
The deduplication process must prioritize approved and synced decisions over recent ones in the comparison set.
The deduplication process must use expanded context window of 200 decisions instead of 50 for more comprehensive duplicate detection.
The system must provide read_all_decisions() as the primary API function for accessing decisions across all branches.
The review command must pre-compute decision branches to optimize performance and ensure correct shard targeting for updates.
Users must be able to migrate from monolithic decision file to sharded layout using plumb migrate command to convert existing decisions.jsonl to decisions/main.jsonl.
The WholeFileSpecUpdater must take full spec content and decisions as input and output section_updates for existing sections and new_sections for brand new sections.
The WholeFileSpecUpdater must accept rewriting whole sections instead of making surgical edits for markdown specs.
The OutlineMerger component must handle structural changes when new sections need to be added or content needs reordering.
The system must include helper functions for DuckDB result type conversion using _clean_duckdb_row() and _to_python_native() functions.
The system must convert DuckDB result types to Python native types for Pydantic compatibility.
The system must implement comprehensive test coverage for migration and merge functionality including edge cases and error conditions.
All LLM-powered functions must be implemented as DSPy programs, not open-ended agents.
Plumb must use the Anthropic Claude SDK (via user's existing account) as its inference provider.
Claude Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5) must serve as the default model for all programs.
Per-program model overrides must be configured in program_models.
Plumb must operate as a git hook and CLI tool without changing how the user writes code.
The commit must be canonical with the pre-commit hook ensuring every committed state has been reviewed and approved.
A commit must represent a fully reconciled snapshot of spec, tests, and code.
Conversation analysis must be opportunistic using Claude Code session data when available and falling back to diff-only analysis when unavailable.
Decisions must still be captured from diff-only analysis even when conversation data is unavailable.
The system must prevent duplicate decisions through multi-stage pipeline using exact matching, Jaccard similarity, and LLM semantic analysis.
Only prescriptive choices affecting system design, behavior, architecture, or data models must be captured as decisions.
Process observations, tooling choices, and diagnostic findings must be filtered out and not captured as decisions.
Spec updates must use search-and-replace approach with edits containing old_text/new_text pairs rather than full section replacement.
Section updates must use exact header matching first, then fall back to normalized matching (stripped whitespace, case-insensitive).
All CLI commands must fail gracefully with clear error message if config.json is missing or malformed.
All DSPy programs must retry on LLM failure (max 2 retries) then raise PlumbInferenceError with human-readable message.
File writes (spec updates, test generation) must use temp file → rename to avoid partial writes.
If conversation log is unavailable, Plumb must continue with diff-only analysis without treating it as an error.
If plumb modify test run fails, Plumb must not stage the modification and must update decision status to rejected_manual.
The git pre-commit hook must call plumb hook command.
The post-commit hook must clear the last_extracted_at timestamp to reset the filter for future extractions.
The system must track which requirements have been modified and send only dirty (changed) requirements to the mapper.
The system must use gitignore-style patterns for ignore functionality with default patterns when no .plumbignore file exists.
Plumb must support file ignore patterns through a '.plumbignore' file.
Plumb must provide a '--all' command option for the 'plumb approve' command to approve all changes at once.
Generated cache and coverage files must be excluded from commits.
The system must include a 'check' command as an alias for manual decision scanning.
Plumb must handle conversations spanning multiple Claude Code session files by reading and merging them chronologically.
Plumb must support exit-and-relaunch scenarios through multi-session file handling.
The sync command must provide progress indicators with status updates to give users feedback during operation.
The workflow must require an explicit sync step after approving decisions.
The workflow must involve staging of sync output before re-committing changes.
The system must use a branch-sharded structure for decision logs.
The system must provide CLI commands for merging decision logs from different branches.
Users must be able to migrate existing decision logs from old monolithic format to new branch-sharded layout through dedicated CLI commands.
The plumb merge-decisions <branch> command must allow users to merge decisions from feature branches back to main.
A find_decision_branch() function must help locate which branch file contains a specific decision ID.
Pattern parsing logic must be modularized into separate functions for reusability across programs.
An extract_outline function must extract markdown headers from content.
The programs module must include token estimation functionality.
The programs module must include chunking functionality.
The programs module must include concurrent mapper functionality to handle large datasets.
The system must break large datasets into token-budget-sized chunks.
The system must use chunked mapping with ThreadPoolExecutor for concurrent processing.
The system must support different merge strategies for result combination.
All documentation files including SKILL files and CLAUDE.md must be kept consistent with same sync workflow requirements.
The API key validation must be implemented as a separate validate_api_access function called before all LLM operations.
All authentication functionality must have comprehensive test coverage.
Existing tests must be updated to mock API validation calls to ensure test suites remain unaffected.
Plumb must support program-specific model configuration through model configuration array in config.json.
The decision log schema requires branch parameter support for decision operations.
Time awareness must use both last_commit datetime and last_extracted_at timestamp as cutoffs, taking the later of the two.
The system must deduplicate decisions across all branches using DuckDB for cross-shard queries.
Within-batch similarity deduplication must prevent duplicate decisions in the same batch.
Plumb must never approve, reject, or edit decisions on the user's behalf without explicit user commands.
All CLI operations must require explicit user commands without automatic synchronization or background operations.
The system must generate complete commit messages after decision review including the list of approved decisions.
Claude Code's skill must read hook output and begin presenting decisions using AskUserQuestion format.
The skill must call appropriate per-decision command (plumb approve, plumb reject, or plumb edit) based on user response.
For rejected decisions, the skill must invoke plumb modify <id> which modifies staged code, runs tests, and reports result conversationally.
For automatic code modification, the skill must verify that plumb modify returns a JSON result containing the modification status and test results.
Once all decisions are resolved, the skill must re-run git commit after the user runs plumb sync.
The hook must fire again after sync, find no pending decisions, exit zero, and allow the commit to land.
Rejected decisions must be marked with 'ignored' status rather than deleted from the system.
The system must detect and handle broken references (rebase) by checking all SHAs in decisions.jsonl against git history.
Unreachable SHAs must be flagged with ref_status: broken and include a warning in output.
The plumb init command must recursively search for markdown files using rglob within directories.
The plumb init command must suggest discovered spec files to the user.
The plumb init command must scan repository for test directories and files to provide suggestions.
The plumb init command must handle test_path as either directory or single file using is_dir() vs is_file() checks.
The plumb init command must skip collection validation for empty test directories to avoid false positives.
The plumb init command must display both stdout and stderr on test collection failure to help user debug.
The plumb init command must fail fast with SystemExit(1) on test collection failure.
The plumb init command must treat infrastructure issues like TimeoutExpired and FileNotFoundError as warnings, not blocking errors.
When multiple session files exist, the system must use most recent session file by modification time or match current session ID.
The system must implement filesystem-safe path sanitization for branch-specific decision log files.
The system must set the last_extracted_at timestamp when writing pending decisions to branch-specific files.
